title: Integrative multi-omics analysis reveals the interaction mechanisms between gut microbiota metabolites and ferroptosis in rheumatoid arthritis.
authors: Liang, Lifang; Liang, Huaguo; He, Min; Zhang, Huiling; Ke, Peifeng
one_liner_zh: 该文用多组学与机器学习筛选RA中铁死亡关键基因GPX3/MYC，并对GPX3与肠道代谢物做分子对接和MD模拟，虽涉及蛋白-小分子互作，但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease characterized by chronic synovitis and joint destruction. To systematically investigate the regulatory relationship between key ferroptosis genes and gut metabolites in RA, this study employed an integrative multi-omics approach combined with machine learning algorithms and single-cell transcriptomic data, identifying and validating GPX3 and MYC as potential critical ferroptosis regulators in RA. METHODS AND RESULTS: First, 16 candidate genes were obtained by intersecting WGCNA, differential expression analysis results, and targets related to ferroptosis and gut microbiota. Following cross-validation with machine learning approaches including LASSO, SVM, and RFE-RF, GPX3 and MYC were ultimately identified as crucial genes. GSVA and GSEA analyses revealed that high expression of GPX3 and MYC was enriched in interferon response and TNFA signaling pathways, while their low expression was associated with fatty acid metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Further single-cell RNA sequencing analysis demonstrated that MYC was expressed in multiple immune cell types, particularly in CD4+ T cells and NK cells. Ferroptosis scoring for CD8+ T cells and subsequent cell communication analysis revealed stronger interactions between CD8+ T cells with higher ferroptosis scores and other immune cells through IFN-II and CCL signaling, further intensifying the activation of the inflammatory microenvironment. Additionally, molecular docking analysis of GPX3 and MYC with the gut metabolites Diosgenin and Differentiation-inducing factor 3 (DIF-3) respectively showed that the GPX3-Diosgenin complex had the lowest binding energy, and a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation was performed on this complex. Results showed good stability of the complex across indicators such as RMSD, RMSF, SASA, and radius of gyration, suggesting that Diosgenin may intervene in ferroptosis and inflammatory injury in RA by binding to and modulating GPX3 function. CONCLUSION: This study elucidated the multifaceted mechanisms of GPX3 and MYC in RA pathogenesis and preliminarily validated the potential role of gut metabolites in mediating ferroptosis regulation, offering novel theoretical foundations and potential strategies for diagnostic biomarker screening and targeted therapy in RA.
abstract_zh: 背景：类风湿关节炎（RA）是一种以慢性滑膜炎和关节破坏为特征的自身免疫性疾病。为系统研究RA中关键铁死亡基因与肠道代谢物之间的调控关系，本研究采用整合多组学方法，结合机器学习算法和单细胞转录组数据，识别并验证了GPX3和MYC作为RA中潜在的关键铁死亡调控因子。方法与结果：首先，通过交集WGCNA、差异表达分析结果以及铁死亡和肠道菌群相关靶点，获得16个候选基因。经LASSO、SVM和RFE-RF等机器学习方法交叉验证后，最终确定GPX3和MYC为关键基因。GSVA和GSEA分析显示，GPX3和MYC的高表达富集于干扰素应答和TNFA信号通路，而其低表达则与脂肪酸代谢和氧化磷酸化通路相关。进一步的单细胞RNA测序分析表明，MYC在多种免疫细胞类型中表达，特别是在CD4+ T细胞和NK细胞中。对CD8+ T细胞进行铁死亡评分及随后的细胞通讯分析显示，铁死亡评分较高的CD8+ T细胞通过IFN-II和CCL信号与其他免疫细胞存在更强的相互作用，进一步加剧了炎症微环境的激活。此外，分别对GPX3和MYC与肠道代谢物薯蓣皂苷（Diosgenin）和分化诱导因子3（DIF-3）进行分子对接分析，结果显示GPX3-薯蓣皂苷复合物的结合能最低，并对此复合物进行了100 ns的分子动力学模拟。结果表明，该复合物在RMSD、RMSF、SASA和回转半径等指标上表现出良好的稳定性，提示薯蓣皂苷可能通过结合并调节GPX3功能来干预RA中的铁死亡和炎症损伤。结论：本研究阐明了GPX3和MYC在RA发病机制中的多方面作用，并初步验证了肠道代谢物在介导铁死亡调控中的潜在角色，为RA的诊断生物标志物筛选和靶向治疗提供了新的理论基础和潜在策略。
